core_obligations: Record the three inputs: the description of the reduction of a formal algebraic space, the construction of the reduced induced closed subspace, and the definition of the completion (proof lines 8080-8086).

Observe that both sides are reduced algebraic spaces satisfying the same mapping property, namely that a morphism from a reduced algebraic space factors through them exactly when its image lies in the closed subset (proof lines 8086-8091).
Conclude that the two agree (proof lines 8091).
proof_roadmap: Comparison of mapping properties and conclusion (proof lines 8086-8091).
difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space X and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts that the reduction of the completion of X along T is the reduced induced closed subspace corresponding to T (statement lines 8072-8078). As in the corresponding statement for an algebraic space, the proof does not compute with the construction of the completion but compares universal properties: it cites the description of the reduction of a formal algebraic space, the definition of the reduced induced closed subspace together with the lemma constructing it, and the definition of the completion, and observes that both sides are reduced algebraic spaces characterised by the same mapping property, namely that a morphism from a reduced algebraic space factors through them exactly when its image lies in T (proof lines 8080-8091). The claim is H2: the argument is an identification of two objects by a common universal property, and each of the three inputs is named rather than left implicit.
